angle: Government-held reserves of critical commodities maintained to buffer supply shocks or military need.

title: Commodity Price Index
angle: Weighted benchmarks such as CRB and GSCI that track broad or sector-specific commodity price levels.

title: Commodity Seasonality
angle: Recurring annual price patterns in commodities driven by harvest cycles, weather, and demand rhythms.

title: Grade and Quality Specifications
angle: How standardized purity or quality grades define deliverable supply and create basis differentials.

title: Commodity Producer Hedging
angle: How miners, farmers, and drillers lock in forward prices to reduce revenue uncertainty.

title: Resource Curse
angle: Paradox where commodity-rich economies underperform due to Dutch Disease and institutional dysfunction.

title: Commodity Trading House
angle: Privately held firms like Glencore and Vitol that dominate global physical commodity flows.

title: Freight Rates and Commodity Markets
angle: How bulk shipping costs, tracked by the Baltic Dry Index, shape delivered commodity prices.

title: Universal Basic Income
angle: How UBI differs from targeted transfers and what pilot experiments reveal about labor-supply effects.

title: Negative Income Tax
angle: Milton Friedman's proposal to replace fragmented welfare with a single phase-out subsidy below a threshold.

title: Means-Testing
angle: How income and asset screens target transfers to the poor while creating welfare cliffs and administrative costs.

title: Welfare Cliff
angle: The implicit marginal tax rate spike where benefit phase-outs create disincentives to increase earnings.

title: Conditional Cash Transfer
angle: Programs like Bolsa Família that tie payments to education or health-check compliance to build human capital.

title: Housing Choice Voucher
angle: Demand-side rental subsidies that let recipients choose private-market units rather than live in public housing.

title: Unemployment Insurance
angle: Payroll-financed temporary income replacement and its role as an automatic stabiliser during downturns.

title: Disability Insurance
angle: Government insurance replacing earnings when workers become unable to work due to long-term impairment.

title: Pay-As-You-Go Pension
angle: How PAYG schemes fund current retirees from active workers' contributions, creating intergenerational fiscal risk.

title: Social Insurance
angle: The contributory framework distinguishing social insurance from pure welfare and the actuarial tensions it raises.

title: In-Kind Transfer
angle: Non-cash government benefits such as food or medical care and the efficiency debate versus direct cash grants.

title: Benefit Notch
angle: A sharp discrete drop in total benefit value at a specific income threshold, contrasted with smooth phase-outs.

title: Good Till Cancelled Order
angle: A resting limit order that persists across sessions until the trader explicitly cancels it.

title: Good Till Date Order
angle: A time-limited order that remains active until a trader-specified calendar date.

title: Immediate or Cancel Order
angle: An order executed instantly for whatever quantity is available, with any remainder cancelled.

title: Market on Close Order
angle: An order guaranteed to execute at the official closing auction price of the session.

title: Market on Open Order
angle: An order routed to the opening auction so it executes at the day's official opening price.

title: Limit on Close Order
angle: A closing-auction order that executes only if the closing price meets the specified limit.

title: Limit on Open Order
angle: An opening-auction order that fills only if the opening price satisfies the limit condition.

title: One Cancels Other Order
angle: A paired order where execution of either leg automatically cancels the remaining leg.

title: Reserve Order
angle: An exchange mechanism that shows only a small visible quantity while a hidden reserve refreshes it.

title: Intermarket Sweep Order
angle: A Reg NMS order type that sweeps multiple venues simultaneously, bypassing the NBBO protection obligation.

title: Dark Limit Order
angle: A non-displayed limit order resting in a dark pool or hidden book with price priority.

title: Primary Peg Order
angle: An order pegged to the same-side best quote, ensuring it never crosses the national best bid or offer.

title: Market Peg Order
angle: An order pegged to the opposite-side best quote, aggressively tracking the far touch of the spread.

title: Conditional Order
angle: An indication-of-interest order that converts to a live order only when matching contra interest is found.

title: Not-Held Order
angle: An instruction granting the broker discretion over timing and price without the client holding them liable.

title: Odd Lot Order
angle: An order for fewer than the standard round-lot size, historically subject to different routing and pricing rules.

title: Cross Order
angle: A broker-facilitated transaction matching a buy and sell from different clients at an agreed price.

title: Basis Order
angle: An order for a stock basket priced at a fixed spread to an index or futures benchmark rather than market.

title: TWAP Order
angle: An execution algorithm slicing a large order into equal time-weighted tranches to match the time-weighted average price.

title: Guaranteed VWAP Order
angle: A broker commitment to fill a client order at the day's volume-weighted average price, absorbing tracking risk.

title: Securitization Revolution
angle: The structural transformation of lending when illiquid loans became tradeable securities.

title: Big Bang Deregulation 1986
angle: How the UK's overnight market liberalisation rewired London as a global financial centre.

title: Rise of Institutional Investors
angle: How pension funds and mutual funds displaced households as the dominant equity owners.

title: Dollar Hegemony
angle: The structural reasons the US dollar retained reserve-currency status after Bretton Woods collapsed.

title: Disintermediation of Banking
angle: How capital markets bypassed commercial banks as the primary channel for corporate finance.

title: Shadow Banking Rise
angle: How non-bank credit intermediaries grew to rival regulated banks in size and systemic importance.

title: Derivatives Market Expansion
angle: The post-1970s explosion of exchange-traded and OTC derivatives as a structural feature of modern finance.

title: Electronic Trading Transition
angle: The decades-long replacement of floor traders and telephone brokers by electronic matching engines.

title: Emerging Market Integration
angle: How developing economies joined global capital markets and absorbed foreign portfolio flows from the 1990s.

title: Private Equity Ascent
angle: The structural shift from public to private ownership as leveraged buyout financing matured after the 1980s.

title: Quantitative Easing Era
angle: How large-scale central bank asset purchases became a standard post-crisis policy tool after 2008.

title: Zero Interest Rate Era
angle: The decade-plus period of near-zero policy rates and its lasting distortions to asset pricing and capital allocation.

title: Index Fund Revolution
angle: The structural shift from active stock-picking to passive index ownership and its effect on price discovery.

title: Floating Exchange Rate Regime
angle: How the post-Bretton Woods world settled on managed floating rather than fixed pegs as the dominant exchange-rate system.

title: European Monetary Union
angle: The structural creation of a shared currency area without a shared fiscal authority and its inherent tensions.

title: China Global Financial Integration
angle: How China's entry into world trade and capital markets restructured global imbalances from the 1990s onward.

title: Junk Bond Market Creation
angle: How Michael Milken's high-yield innovations opened capital markets to below-investment-grade borrowers in the 1970s–80s.

title: Shareholder Value Movement
angle: The ideological and structural shift that made maximising shareholder returns the dominant corporate objective.

title: Marginal Value at Risk
angle: Measures how adding a small position changes a portfolio's overall VaR.

title: Component Value at Risk
angle: Decomposes total portfolio VaR into each holding's standalone risk contribution.

title: Tail Dependence Coefficient
angle: Quantifies the probability that two assets crash simultaneously in extreme events.

title: Copula Risk Modeling
angle: Uses copula functions to capture non-linear dependence between asset losses.

title: Risk Contribution Decomposition
angle: Attributes total portfolio risk to individual positions using Euler's homogeneity theorem.

title: Maximum Drawdown
angle: Captures the largest peak-to-trough loss as a standalone risk measure for portfolios.

title: Spectral Risk Measure
angle: Generalizes expected shortfall by weighting tail losses according to investor risk aversion.

title: Distortion Risk Measure
angle: Transforms the loss probability distribution using a distortion function to price tail risk.

title: Coherent Risk Measure
angle: Defines the axiomatic properties (subadditivity, monotonicity, homogeneity) a valid risk measure must satisfy.

title: Semi-Variance
angle: Measures downside volatility by squaring only below-mean or below-target returns.

title: Lower Partial Moment
angle: Generalizes semi-variance by raising downside deviations to any chosen order.

title: Modified Value at Risk
angle: Adjusts parametric VaR for skewness and excess kurtosis using the Cornish-Fisher expansion.

title: Risk Factor Sensitivity
angle: Measures how portfolio value changes for a unit shift in each underlying market risk factor.

title: Loss Given Default
angle: Estimates the fraction of an exposure actually lost when a borrower defaults.

title: Probability of Default
angle: Estimates the likelihood a borrower will fail to meet obligations over a defined horizon.

title: Exposure at Default
angle: Measures the outstanding credit exposure at the moment a counterparty defaults.

title: VaR Backtesting
angle: Validates VaR models by comparing predicted loss thresholds against realized trading losses.

title: Kupiec Proportion-of-Failures Test
angle: Tests whether a VaR model's exception rate is statistically consistent with its confidence level.

title: Christoffersen Interval Forecast Test
angle: Checks both the frequency and independence of VaR violations over a backtesting window.

title: Tracking Error Volatility
angle: Measures the standard deviation of a portfolio's returns relative to its benchmark.

title: Risk-Adjusted Return on Capital
angle: Scales a business line's profit by the economic capital allocated to absorb its losses.

title: IPO Pricing Mechanism
angle: How underwriters set the final offer price from the bookbuild range to the public.

title: Stabilisation Trading
angle: Post-IPO underwriter open-market purchases that smooth the share price in the aftermarket.

title: Rights Issue
angle: A renounceable offer of new shares to existing holders at a discount to defend ownership pro-rata.

title: Accelerated Bookbuild
angle: An overnight institutional placement that raises equity without a full roadshow or prospectus.

title: Best-Efforts Offering
angle: An underwriting structure where the bank sells as many shares as possible without guaranteeing proceeds.

title: Prospectus
angle: The legally required disclosure document that accompanies a public equity offering to potential investors.

title: Red Herring Prospectus
angle: A preliminary prospectus filed before pricing that omits the final offer price and share count.

title: Regulation A+ Offering
angle: A US mini-IPO exemption allowing smaller issuers to raise up to $75 million from retail investors.

title: Regulation D Offering
angle: The SEC safe harbour for exempt private placements primarily to accredited investors.

title: Equity Crowdfunding Offering
angle: Regulation CF-governed raises from the general public through an online funding portal.

title: SPAC IPO
angle: The initial blank-cheque offering that capitalises a SPAC before any acquisition target is identified.

title: Tender Offer
angle: A public invitation for shareholders to sell or exchange their shares at a specified price within a deadline.

title: Block Trade
angle: A privately negotiated sale of a large shareholding outside the open market, typically via a broker.

title: Registered Direct Offering
angle: A hybrid structure placing shares with select institutions using an existing shelf registration without a public roadshow.

title: Warrant Offering
angle: The issuance of standalone warrants giving holders the right to buy new shares at a fixed exercise price.

title: Standby Underwriting
angle: An arrangement where underwriters commit to subscribe any unexercised rights in a rights issue.

title: Clawback Provision
angle: An IPO allocation clause that transfers shares from institutional to retail tranches if public demand is strong.

title: Cornerstone Investor
angle: An anchor institution that commits to a fixed IPO allocation pre-listing in exchange for a lock-up period.

title: Directed Share Program
angle: An IPO carve-out reserving shares at the offer price for employees, customers, or other designated individuals.

title: Dual-Track Process
angle: Running an IPO preparation and a private M&A sale simultaneously to maximise a seller's exit optionality.

title: John Neff
angle: Windsor Fund's low-P/E contrarian who outperformed the market for three decades.

title: Michael Price
angle: Aggressive value investor known for distressed-debt activism and Mutual Series funds.

title: Mario Gabelli
angle: GAMCO founder who popularized private-market-value analysis for undervalued industrials.

title: David Dreman
angle: Contrarian investing theorist who documented how low-P/E stocks systematically beat expectations.

title: Irving Kahn
angle: Graham protégé who invested into his hundreds, exemplifying patient deep-value discipline.

title: Walter Schloss
angle: One-man deep-value shop that compounded at 16% annually for nearly five decades without a computer.

title: Martin Whitman
angle: Third Avenue founder who focused on safe-and-cheap assets in distressed and overlooked securities.

title: Bill Miller
angle: Legg Mason manager who beat the S&P 500 fifteen consecutive years before a dramatic reversal.

title: François Rochon
angle: Quebec-based concentrated investor who blends Graham fundamentals with qualitative moat analysis.

title: Li Lu
angle: Himalaya Capital founder and Munger-endorsed investor who pioneered deep-value investing in Asia.

title: Prem Watsa
angle: Fairfax Financial chairman known as Canada's Buffett for pairing insurance float with value equity picks.

title: Irving Fisher
angle: Yale economist whose debt-deflation theory emerged from his own catastrophic 1929 market call.

title: John Train
angle: Author of The Money Masters who documented the methods of ten great investors and shaped a generation.

title: Templeton's Contrarian Methodology
angle: How Templeton systematically bought at points of maximum pessimism to find global bargains.

title: Edward Thorp
angle: Mathematician who applied card-counting probability to warrant arbitrage and early quant hedge funds.

title: Ralph Wanger
angle: Acorn Fund manager who specialized in small-cap growth with a narrative, theme-driven approach.

title: Shelby Cullom Davis
angle: Insurance-stock specialist who built a fortune from $50,000 by concentrating in undervalued insurers.

title: John Bogle
angle: Vanguard founder who built the first retail index fund and became the industry's fiercest cost crusader.

title: T. Rowe Price Jr.
angle: Pioneer of growth-stock investing who argued quality companies compound better than cheap ones.

title: Nick Sleep
angle: Nomad Partnership manager whose scale-economy-shared thesis generated exceptional long-run returns.

title: David Abrams
angle: Low-turnover, concentrated value manager whose Boston fund compounded quietly for two decades.

title: Chuck Akre
angle: Akre Capital founder who built his framework around the three-legged stool of compounders.

title: Tom Russo
angle: Gardner Russo partner who specialises in global consumer brands with reinvestment capacity.

title: Payment Versus Delivery
angle: The settlement principle ensuring a securities transfer occurs only if the cash leg simultaneously clears.

title: Trade Repository
angle: Regulated data warehouses that aggregate OTC derivatives transaction reports for systemic-risk surveillance.

title: Self-Regulatory Organisation
angle: Industry bodies like FINRA that exercise delegated governmental authority to write and enforce member conduct rules.

title: Index Provider
angle: Firms such as MSCI and FTSE Russell whose methodologies govern trillions in passive investment mandates.

title: Global Custodian
angle: Banks that safekeep cross-border securities, manage corporate actions, and co-ordinate a network of sub-custodians.

title: Long Straddle
angle: Buying both a call and put at the same strike to profit from large moves in either direction.

title: Short Straddle
angle: Selling both a call and put at the same strike to collect premium when price stays flat.

title: Long Strangle
angle: Buying out-of-the-money call and put at different strikes for cheaper volatility exposure than a straddle.

title: Short Strangle
angle: Selling OTM call and put to earn premium with a wider breakeven band than a short straddle.

title: Jade Lizard
angle: Combining a short put with a short call spread so total premium collected exceeds the call spread width.

title: Reverse Jade Lizard
angle: Combining a short call with a short put spread so total credit eliminates upside risk entirely.

title: Christmas Tree Spread
angle: A three-strike extension of a butterfly where one wing is split across two further-out strikes.

title: Condor Spread
angle: Four-legged spread using four different strikes that profits when the underlying stays in a wide range.

title: Broken Wing Butterfly
angle: An asymmetric butterfly with unequal wing widths that eliminates risk on one side in exchange for a credit.

title: Skip-Strike Butterfly
angle: A butterfly variant that skips one strike between the body and one wing to create directional bias.

title: Double Diagonal Spread
angle: Selling near-term OTM options and buying further-dated OTM options on both sides simultaneously.

title: Call Backspread
angle: Selling fewer ATM calls and buying more OTM calls to profit from explosive upside moves.

title: Put Backspread
angle: Selling fewer ATM puts and buying more OTM puts to benefit from sharp downside moves.

title: Reverse Calendar Spread
angle: Buying the near-term option and selling the longer-dated one to profit from an imminent volatility spike.

title: Double Calendar Spread
angle: Placing calendar spreads at two different strikes simultaneously to widen the profit tent.

title: Synthetic Covered Call
angle: Replicating a covered call using long deep-in-the-money call plus short OTM call without holding shares.

title: Risk Reversal
angle: Simultaneously buying an OTM call and selling an OTM put to gain directional exposure at low net premium.

title: Fence Strategy
angle: A three-legged collar variant that uses a short OTM call, long ATM put, and long underlying to define a payoff range.

title: Long Combo
angle: Buying an OTM call and selling an OTM put to create leveraged bullish exposure with little or no net premium.

title: Short Combo
angle: Selling an OTM call and buying an OTM put to create leveraged bearish exposure with little net premium.

title: Strap Strategy
angle: Buying two calls and one put at the same strike to bet on a large move with upside bias.

title: Strip Strategy
angle: Buying two puts and one call at the same strike to bet on a large move with downside bias.

title: Split-Strike Synthetic
angle: A synthetic long stock using options at different strikes to reduce cost at the expense of a gap risk zone.

title: Securities Act of 1933 Enactment
angle: How Congress's first federal securities law imposed mandatory disclosure to end fraudulent stock sales.

title: Securities Exchange Act of 1934 Enactment
angle: How the 1934 law created the SEC and established ongoing reporting obligations for public companies.

title: Investment Company Act of 1940 Enactment
angle: How this New Deal-era law set the governance and disclosure rules that still define mutual funds today.

title: Basel I Capital Accord Adoption
angle: How the 1988 Basel Accord created the first internationally agreed minimum bank capital ratio.

title: MiFID I Implementation
angle: How the 2007 Markets in Financial Instruments Directive dismantled exchange monopolies across Europe.

title: Commodity Futures Modernization Act Passage
angle: How the 2000 law exempted OTC derivatives from oversight and set the stage for the 2008 crisis.

title: FIRREA Passage
angle: How the 1989 Financial Institutions Reform Act dismantled the thrift industry after the S&L collapse.

title: JOBS Act Passage
angle: How the 2012 law reopened public markets to small companies by loosening IPO and crowdfunding rules.

title: Short-Selling Ban of 2008
angle: How regulators in the US and Europe imposed emergency bans on financial-stock short sales during the crisis.

title: Regulation Best Interest Adoption
angle: How the SEC's 2019 rule replaced the suitability standard with a stricter best-interest obligation for brokers.

title: Plaza Accord Signing
angle: How the 1985 G5 agreement at the Plaza Hotel engineered a coordinated dollar depreciation.

title: FATF Creation
angle: How the G7's 1989 task force built the global anti-money-laundering framework still enforced today.

title: Blank Check Preferred
angle: Authorized preferred stock whose terms the board may set at issuance without shareholder approval.

title: PIK Preferred Stock
angle: Preferred shares that pay dividends in additional shares rather than cash, deferring cash outflows.

title: Trust Preferred Securities
angle: Hybrid instruments issued by a bank-sponsored trust that blend debt tax treatment with Tier 1 capital credit.

title: Auction Rate Preferred
angle: Preferred stock whose dividend rate resets periodically via a Dutch auction among existing holders.

title: Exchangeable Preferred Stock
angle: Preferred stock the issuer may swap for debt securities at its option on specified terms.

title: Fixed-to-Floating Preferred
angle: Preferred stock that pays a fixed dividend for a set period, then resets to a floating benchmark rate.

title: Deferred Shares
angle: Shares that rank behind ordinary shares for dividends and capital, often used to restructure founder economics.

title: Alphabet Shares
angle: Separate share classes labeled A, B, C and so on, allowing flexible dividend allocation among different shareholders.

title: Profit Interest Units
angle: LLC equity class that entitles holders to a share of future appreciation only, without immediate taxable income.

title: Stapled Securities
angle: Two or more securities permanently bound together and traded as one unit, common in Australian listed trusts.

title: Phantom Stock Plan
angle: A cash-settled incentive that mirrors share value appreciation without issuing actual equity to participants.

title: Authorized but Unissued Shares
angle: Shares approved in the charter but not yet sold, representing potential future dilution for existing shareholders.

title: Sunset Provision
angle: A charter clause that automatically collapses super-voting shares to one-share-one-vote after a trigger event.

title: Full Ratchet Anti-Dilution
angle: An anti-dilution mechanism that reprices preferred to the lowest subsequent issuance price regardless of round size.

title: Broad-Based Weighted Average
angle: The most founder-friendly anti-dilution formula, averaging new and old prices weighted by all dilutive securities.

title: Narrow-Based Weighted Average
angle: A weighted-average anti-dilution formula that counts only issued preferred shares, producing a sharper reset than broad-based.

title: Restricted Voting Shares
angle: Shares with a fractional vote per share rather than zero votes, maintaining partial influence for public shareholders.

title: Multiple Voting Shares
angle: Shares carrying more than one vote each, the Canadian and European equivalent of US high-vote stock.

title: Redeemable Ordinary Shares
angle: Common shares that can be bought back by the company at a predetermined price, used mainly in UK private companies.

title: Management Shares
angle: A share class reserved for company founders or managers carrying disproportionate voting control at incorporation.

title: Series Seed Preferred
angle: A simplified preferred share class used in early-stage startup financings before a full Series A round.

title: Simple Agreement for Future Equity
angle: A convertible instrument that grants rights to future equity on a priced round without accruing interest or a maturity date.

title: Shadow Equity Plan
angle: A notional ownership scheme for private-company employees that mirrors equity economics without conferring legal ownership.

title: Non-Participating Preferred
angle: Preferred stock that receives its liquidation preference but does not share further in remaining proceeds alongside common.

title: Business Cycle Rotation
angle: Mapping equity sector weights to the four phases of the economic cycle.

title: Factor Rotation
angle: Systematically shifting exposure among equity factors as macro conditions change.

title: Fixed-Income Rotation
angle: Shifting duration, credit quality, or bond-sector weights in response to rate cycles.

title: Currency Rotation
angle: Reallocating across currency blocs or currency-hedged sleeves based on macro signals.

title: Commodity Sector Rotation
angle: Moving between energy, metals, and agricultural commodities as macro regimes shift.

title: Inter-Asset-Class Rotation
angle: Dynamically reweighting equities, bonds, real assets, and cash across market regimes.

title: Tactical Asset Allocation Rotation
angle: Short-term deviations from strategic weights driven by valuation and momentum signals.

title: Relative Strength Rotation
angle: Rotating into the highest-ranked assets by relative price strength against a universe.

title: Yield Curve Rotation
angle: Repositioning bond duration as the slope between short and long rates shifts.

title: Risk-On Risk-Off Rotation
angle: Switching between high-beta and safe-haven assets driven by investor risk appetite.

title: Industry Group Rotation
angle: Rotating at the industry-group level below broad sectors for finer cycle positioning.

title: Volatility Regime Rotation
angle: Adjusting strategy exposure as markets transition between low- and high-volatility regimes.

title: Collective Action Clause
angle: How a bond contract provision lets a supermajority of creditors bind holdouts to a restructuring.

title: Holdout Creditors
angle: Bondholders who refuse debt exchanges and pursue full repayment through litigation, complicating sovereign restructurings.

title: London Club
angle: The informal creditor group that renegotiates sovereign commercial bank debt outside official government channels.

title: Original Sin (Sovereign Debt)
angle: Why emerging-market governments struggle to borrow internationally in their own currency, amplifying default risk.

title: Sovereign Debt Overhang
angle: How an excessive debt stock suppresses investment and growth by transferring future returns to creditors.

title: Sudden Stop
angle: The abrupt reversal of capital inflows that triggers liquidity crises and forces sovereign adjustment.

title: Pari Passu Clause
angle: The sovereign bond covenant requiring equal treatment of creditors, famously weaponised in Argentina's default litigation.

title: IMF Conditionality
angle: The policy reforms a borrowing government must implement in exchange for IMF programme disbursements.

title: HIPC Initiative
angle: The multilateral programme that wrote down heavily indebted poor countries' debts to sustainable levels from 1996 onward.

title: GDP-Linked Bonds
angle: Sovereign instruments whose coupon or principal tracks economic output, sharing default risk with creditors.

title: Sovereign Debt Contagion
angle: How a single sovereign default spreads borrowing stress to unrelated countries through investor panic and correlation.

title: Notes to Financial Statements
angle: How footnote disclosures expand and qualify the numbers in the primary statements.

title: Proxy Statement
angle: The SEC filing that discloses executive pay, board votes, and related-party transactions to shareholders.

title: 10-Q
angle: The quarterly SEC filing that provides condensed unaudited financials between annual 10-K reports.

title: Statement of Retained Earnings
angle: The reconciliation of opening to closing retained earnings through net income and dividends.

title: Comparative Financial Statements
angle: The requirement to present prior-period figures alongside current results for trend analysis.

title: Interim Financial Statements
angle: The special recognition and measurement rules that apply when reporting for periods shorter than a full year.

title: Restatement of Financial Statements
angle: When and how a company corrects previously issued financials for errors or fraud discoveries.

title: Management Discussion and Analysis
angle: The MD&A section where executives explain results, liquidity, and forward-looking risks in narrative form.

title: Discontinued Operations Reporting
angle: How divested or held-for-sale business units are carved out and presented separately on the income statement.

title: Variable Interest Entity
angle: The consolidation rules that pull off-balance-sheet SPEs onto a sponsor's balance sheet under ASC 810.

title: Push-Down Accounting
angle: Revaluing an acquired subsidiary's standalone financial statements to reflect the acquirer's purchase price.

title: Noncontrolling Interest
angle: How the portion of a subsidiary not owned by the parent is presented in consolidated equity and earnings.

title: Functional Currency Translation
angle: How a subsidiary's foreign-currency financials are translated into the parent's reporting currency.

title: Prior Period Adjustment
angle: The retrospective correction of an accounting error directly to opening retained earnings, bypassing current income.

title: Heston Stochastic Volatility Model
angle: How the Heston model lets volatility itself follow a mean-reverting random process, fitting the volatility smile.

title: SABR Model
angle: The SABR model prices interest-rate options by making both forward price and volatility stochastic simultaneously.

title: Local Volatility Model
angle: Dupire's framework calibrates a deterministic vol surface so the model perfectly matches all observed option prices.

title: Black-76 Model
angle: Fischer Black's adaptation of Black-Scholes to price futures options and interest-rate caps and floors.

title: Bachelier Model
angle: The normal-distribution option pricing model, preferred for near-zero or negative underlying rates.

title: Jump-Diffusion Model
angle: Merton's extension of Black-Scholes that adds sudden price jumps to capture fat-tailed return distributions.

title: Variance Gamma Model
angle: A pure-jump Levy process option pricing model that independently controls skewness and excess kurtosis.

title: Constant Elasticity of Variance Model
angle: The CEV model links volatility inversely to stock price level, generating the observed leverage effect.

title: Trinomial Option Pricing
angle: The trinomial lattice adds a middle node at each step, improving convergence and handling American exercise.

title: Finite Difference Methods for Options
angle: Numerical PDE solvers — explicit, implicit, and Crank-Nicolson — that discretise the Black-Scholes equation on a grid.

title: Risk-Neutral Pricing
angle: The foundational theorem establishing that derivatives are priced by discounting expected payoffs under a risk-neutral measure.

title: Forward Measure
angle: How changing the numeraire to a zero-coupon bond simplifies interest-rate derivative pricing under the T-forward measure.

title: Bjerksund-Stensland Model
angle: An analytic approximation for American option pricing that avoids the full binomial lattice computational cost.

title: Barone-Adesi Whaley Model
angle: A quadratic approximation for American option fair value widely used by practitioners for its closed-form speed.

title: Volatility Surface Construction
angle: How traders build a consistent three-dimensional implied-volatility surface across strikes and expiries for pricing and hedging.

title: Stochastic Local Volatility Model
angle: A hybrid that blends local and stochastic volatility to match the smile while reproducing realistic forward dynamics.

title: Rough Volatility Model
angle: Gatheral's fractional Brownian motion framework, where volatility paths are rougher than standard diffusion implies.

title: Copula Pricing Model
angle: How copula functions model joint default or asset-return dependence to price basket and correlation derivatives.

title: LIBOR Market Model
angle: The Brace-Gatarek-Musiela framework that models forward LIBOR rates directly for cap, floor, and swaption pricing.

title: Hull-White Model
angle: A one-factor short-rate model with mean reversion that fits the initial yield curve for interest-rate derivatives.

title: Cox-Ingersoll-Ross Model
angle: The CIR model keeps interest rates non-negative through a square-root diffusion term for the short rate.

title: Displaced Diffusion Model
angle: A simple shift of the lognormal Black model that accommodates negative interest rates without switching to a full normal model.

title: Quanto Pricing
angle: How the correlation between an underlying asset and an exchange rate is incorporated into quanto derivative valuation.

title: Exotic Option Monte Carlo Simulation
angle: Path-dependent payoff estimation via simulation, covering variance reduction techniques such as antithetic variates and control variates.

title: Least-Squares Monte Carlo
angle: Longstaff-Schwartz regression-based method for valuing American and Bermudan options on simulated paths.

title: Execution Risk
angle: The risk that a trade cannot be filled at its intended price, size, or timing.

title: Volatility Risk
angle: The exposure of options and structured products to unexpected changes in implied volatility.

title: Correlation Breakdown Risk
angle: The tendency for assumed asset correlations to spike toward one during market stress, wrecking diversification.

title: Political Risk
angle: Investment losses stemming from government actions, policy reversals, expropriation, or civil instability.

title: Cyber Risk
angle: Financial losses and operational disruption caused by data breaches, ransomware, and system intrusions.

title: Vendor Risk
angle: Operational and financial exposure arising from reliance on third-party service providers and outsourcing.

title: Pipeline Risk
angle: The market exposure a bank carries on committed but unhedged loan or bond underwriting positions.

title: Demographic Risk
angle: Long-run liability mismatches in pension and insurance portfolios driven by unexpected longevity or mortality trends.

title: Commodity Risk
angle: Corporate and portfolio exposure to price swings in raw materials, energy, and agricultural inputs.
